parsed_product.description: The Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Omni arrived in Australia in March 2026, marking a significant advancement in the brand’s flagship automated cleaning lineup. With a recommended retail price of $2,299, this model is engineered to provide a comprehensive, hands-off maintenance solution for the entire home, moving beyond simple vacuuming to include high-pressure scrubbing and sophisticated self-maintenance. It represents a shift toward "set and forget" technology, where the hardware manages its own hygiene, water levels, and debris disposal through a highly integrated base station.  At the core of its cleaning capability is a vacuum system that produces a class-leading 13,000 pascals of suction. This extreme pressure is specifically designed to address the challenges of Australian households with mixed flooring, as it can effectively pull fine dust and pet dander from the deepest layers of thick-pile carpets. The main brush is constructed with a zero-tangle design, utilizing a dual-comb structure that prevents long hair and fur from wrapping around the roller, ensuring consistent performance without the need for manual cutting or cleaning. When transitioning to carpets, the robot utilizes ultrasonic sensors to instantly boost suction power while raising its mopping pads by 15 millimetres to keep fabrics completely dry.  The mopping functionality is handled by the Ozmo Turbo 3.0 system, which employs dual-rotating pads that apply constant downward pressure at 180 revolutions per minute. This mechanical action is far more effective at removing dried-on kitchen spills and muddy footprints than static vibrating pads. To ensure no area is left untouched, the TruEdge Adaptive Edge Mopping technology allows the robot to extend its mopping pad physically when it nears a wall or a corner. This ensures the pads reach within 1 millimetre of skirting boards, effectively eliminating the uncleaned border often seen with previous generations of robotic hardware.  The Omni station is a central part of the user experience, designed to automate almost every aspect of the device's upkeep. After each cleaning cycle, the station washes the mop pads with 70°C hot water to dissolve oils and eliminate household bacteria. This is followed by a hot-air drying cycle that prevents the growth of mould and the development of unpleasant odours in the home. The station also automatically empties the robot’s dustbin into a 3-litre sealed bag, which can hold up to 90 days of dust, and refills the robot’s internal water tank from a 4-litre reservoir. To maintain hygiene, the station includes a silver ion sterilisation module that treats the water supply, ensuring the floors are cleaned with sanitised water.  Navigation is powered by the AIVI 3D 3.0 system, which combines dToF (Direct Time-of-Flight) laser scanning with a high-definition AI camera. This allows the robot to map a home's layout in seconds and identify over 45 types of common household objects, from stray cables and shoes to pet bowls and socks. This level of environmental awareness ensures the robot can navigate complex rooms without getting stuck or requiring human intervention to clear its path. Through the Ecovacs Home app, users can access a 3D map of their residence, set "no-go" zones, and even use the robot as a mobile home security camera to check in on pets or the house while away.  Longevity is supported by a 5,200 mAh battery that provides up to 210 minutes of continuous cleaning, making it well-suited for larger Australian suburban homes. The software experience is further enhanced by the YIKO 2.0 voice assistant, which allows users to direct the robot to specific rooms or even to clean around a particular piece of furniture using natural language commands. By combining extreme suction power with a self-sufficient maintenance hub and highly precise navigation, the T90 Pro Omni offers an uncompromising approach to modern domestic cleanliness.
